model: fixed data contract, flexible conversation — ask only what can't be inferred; confirm inferences, never assume; visitor corrections always win

questions.copy: What do you need help solving today?
questions.copyAfterOpener: Got it — “{said}”. So I point that at the right product, which of these is closest?
questions.chipsNote: The client's own list, Sep 2: competitive analysis, Awareness, Leads, Sales, then free text — three of the four in Meta's ad-objective words verbatim (Awareness, Leads, Sales), with competitive analysis first because Meta has no objective for it and it is the demo's strongest opening. Meta's Traffic and Engagement rows are deliberately not offered: AI-search visibility and creator programs are still reachable through 'Something else', the chat and /products, they are simply not one of the four doors. Each row is a routing domain; what the word means HERE lives in hero.byDomain[domain] — the detail pane is what keeps 'Leads' and 'Sales' from reading as paid media.
questions.notes: Free text can carry multiple domains at once — that is how multi-product opportunities surface.
questions.skipWhen: entry came from a product ad (product_interest pre-filled; opener names the product)
questions.copyUnclassified: I didn't catch a marketing problem in that — which of these is closest? Or describe it another way.
questions.copyUnclassifiedNote: Shown when free text at q1 classifies to no domain. Asking the identical question again read as a loop (QA, Sep 2: emoji and gibberish got the same words back with no acknowledgement).
questions.moreChipsNote: Every routing domain that is not one of the four rows, offered as a chip under 'Something else' so every product has a visible door while the picker keeps its four-row Meta shape (client, Sep 2, option c). A tap is a deterministic q1 answer — flow.js domainFromLabel and convo.js matchingChip read this list too — and the label is what the visitor's bubble says.

questions.copy: Got it. What's your company? A website works — I'll start pulling your snapshot together.

confirmMode.when: the landing chooser read a domain out of the visitor's business email and they never typed a site themselves — questions.json's own model line: confirm inferences, never assume
confirmMode.copy: Your email puts you at {domain} — is that the site I should read?

questions.sideEffect: starts background research (size, industry, competitors, AI-search presence) and the snapshot build — from a website, or from a bare company name. An email-derived domain starts nothing until the visitor confirms it.
questions.skipWhen: the visitor's first message included a website — they typed it, so there is nothing to confirm

confirmMode.when: research recognised the company and knows its headcount — copyNoIndustry renders when the model gave no industry
confirmMode.copy: Looks like {company} is around {employees} people, in {industry} — did I get that right?
confirmMode.copyNoIndustry: Looks like {company} is around {employees} people — did I get that right?

askMode.copy: Roughly how big is the company?

questions.copy: When do you want this working — this quarter, this year, or just exploring?
questions.copyWithGoal: So you want to {goal} — when do you want that working: this quarter, this year, or just exploring?

questions.skipWhen: the solution match is already obvious from prior answers

brand_health.copy: How do you track your brand today — an agency, in-house dashboards, or not really yet?
brand_health.decides: always-on tracking subscription vs. deeper analytics; upgrade path

competitive.copy: Who are you measuring against — competitors you name, or the whole category?
competitive.copyWithPeers: I'm seeing {competitors} as your closest comparison set — is that who you're measuring against?
competitive.peersNote: the {competitors} form is only ever asked when research came back with the visitor's REAL comparison set — never with the seeded fallback names (machine/flow.js q6View)

leads.copy: Where do most of your inbound leads land today — a form, a phone line, or a shared inbox?
leads.decides: which channel the agents answer first; telephony vs. CRM integration leads the scoping

research.copy: Is this a one-off study, or something you'll run regularly?
research.decides: self-service platform vs. serviced research; trial-readiness

business_impact.copy: Who needs convincing — the board, the CFO, or your own team?
business_impact.decides: seniority of the sale; executive audience biases consultative

audiences.copy: Where does your first-party data live — a CDP, a data warehouse, or mostly in the ad platforms?
audiences.decides: data readiness; demo now vs. consultative scoping

influencer.copy: Roughly how many creators do you work with in a year?
influencer.decides: SMB platform vs. enterprise program (~100+ creators)

reputation.copy: Are you watching one market, or monitoring globally in multiple languages?
reputation.decides: early-warning narrative intelligence vs. global media monitoring

ai_visibility.copy: Which platforms matter most to you — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity?

marketing_ops.copy: Which part of the workflow feels most fragmented — planning, creation, media, or measurement?

ai_workspace.copy: Where is AI use in the team today — a few personal licences, everyone on their own tools, or nothing sanctioned yet?
ai_workspace.decides: whether the conversation is about consolidation, governance or a first rollout

sample_quality.copy: Is this sample for your own studies, or sample you buy on behalf of clients?
sample_quality.decides: agency volume vs. single-brand supply; who signs the contract

hero.model: the landing is a chooser, not a blank prompt — the visitor picks what they are solving, gives a business email, and lands in the conversation with that first answer already given (client, Sep 1, after Meta's ad-objective flow)
hero.eyebrow: Stagwell.AI · Agentic solutions built by marketing experts for modern marketers
hero.title: What do you need help solving today?
hero.sub: Pick what you're up against, or just leave your email — the agent reads your brand and finds your fit.
hero.subNote: Says out loud that the row is optional. Kept under ~105 characters: past that it wraps to a second line at 1280×720 and the card falls below the fold.
hero.emptyImageAlt: How the agent works: it reads AI search and brand signals, understands your brand, sees where you stand, finds the right opportunities and recommends what to do next — producing performance and opportunity reads.
hero.emptyImageNote: the client's own artwork (source PNG beside it at agent.png, 1536x1024; the .webp is that file at 1100px and 30KB). machine/hero.js prefers this over its built-in drawing — set to null to go back to the SVG, which is composed from emptySays and emptySteps below.
hero.emptySays: I analyze your brand and find the areas where AI can help most.
hero.emptyTitle: Pick one and I'll show you what it covers.
hero.emptyLine: Whichever you choose, the agent reads your brand first — where you stand, how AI assistants describe you, where your signal is moving — then names the products that fit.
hero.emailHint: We read your company from its domain — that's how the analysis starts before you answer another question.
hero.errorsNote: The address is the only thing either front door refuses over — a picked row (or a typed description) is an accelerator, and its absence is answered by the agent asking, never by a refusal.

errors.noEmail: We need your business email to get started. The agent reads your company from its domain, and your report goes back to it.
errors.badEmail: That doesn't look like an email address yet — check it over.
errors.personalEmail: That's a personal address. Use your work email — the agent reads your company from its domain, and there's nothing to analyse behind a personal one.

hero.otherLine: Describe the problem in your own words, or paste your website. The agent reads it, works out which products fit, and asks only what it can't infer.
hero.otherPlaceholder: Describe your problem — or paste your website, like nike.com
otherGoodFor: More than one problem at once

brand_health.title: How is my brand really doing?
brand_health.line: Track awareness, consideration and momentum every day — and watch a campaign actually move them, instead of waiting for the next quarterly read.

competitive.title: How do I stack up against my competitors?
competitive.line: See where you gain and lose ground against the rivals you name — share, perception and momentum, measured against them rather than in isolation.

ai_visibility.title: How do AI models describe my brand?
ai_visibility.line: Find out how ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity describe and recommend you versus your rivals — and what to change so you show up more.

influencer.title: How do I run creator programs that pay back?
influencer.line: Run creator programs end to end — discovery and vetting, then outreach, contracts, approvals and tracking through to ROI.

leads.title: How many hand-raises are we losing?
leads.line: Answer, qualify and book every inbound lead the moment it arrives — voice and chat agents working any hour and any language, handing anything they can't finish to a person with the context already gathered.

audiences.title: How do I reach better audiences?
audiences.line: Turn your first-party data into audiences you can actually buy — built, enriched and activated straight into your channels.

research.title: How do I run research myself, fast?
research.line: Describe what you want to learn; AI drafts the questionnaire, fields it to respondents in 100+ countries and helps you read the results — in days, no agency required.

business_impact.title: How do I prove the brand is moving the business?
business_impact.line: Continuous scoring of the emotional and functional drivers of brand strength, tied to pricing power, revenue and market value — the numbers a CFO and a board will accept.

reputation.title: How do I see a reputation risk before it becomes a story?
reputation.line: Reads narrative alignment and emotional intensity across the conversation about you, and flags the risks that are about to become headlines.

media_monitoring.title: How do I monitor everything said about us, globally?
media_monitoring.line: Human-plus-AI monitoring of news, social and broadcast worldwide, in every language, with analysis of the narratives your stakeholders are forming.

real_world_behavior.title: How do I measure what people actually do?
real_world_behavior.line: Real-world behaviour — who visited, how foot traffic moved, and whether your advertising changed where people went — instead of what they tell a survey.

marketing_ops.title: How do I get my marketing tools working as one system?
marketing_ops.line: Connect planning, creation, media and measurement into an agentic operating system that keeps learning, with specialised machines for media, knowledge and targeting.

ai_workspace.title: How do I give the whole team AI, safely?
ai_workspace.line: One login, one contract and one security standard for the frontier models and purpose-built marketing assistants — with uploaded data never used to train the models.
goodFor: One contract, not a drawer of subscriptions

sample_quality.title: How do I know the people behind my research are real?
sample_quality.line: Verified consumer and B2B respondents from a global supply and identity backbone, so every study stands on sample you can trust.

captureMoment.when: at the snapshot reveal — never before
captureMoment.emailCopy: Get the full report — and keep it updated.
captureMoment.consentLine: By sending, you agree someone from Stagwell can follow up about these results.

captureMoment.bandTitle: One read. The whole suite behind it.
captureMoment.bandAccent: The next step is the people who run them.
captureMoment.bandSub: Brand tracking, competitive benchmarking, creator marketing, AI-search visibility, consumer research, voice agents — matched to your problem by strategists who work with them every day.
captureMoment.bandNote: kept deliberately distinct from the landing CTA band lower on the same page

humanAck: Got it — I'll make sure a person picks this up; the route at the end books that. A couple more quick answers so they arrive already briefed.
humanAckAfterDone: Of course. Open your snapshot and take the “Book a demo” or “Talk to an AI expert” button, or leave a number and Stagwell.AI will call you — either way a person, not a script.
humanAckNote: Spoken the moment override 4 fires (a human ask at any question) and again if it arrives after the read is finished. QA (Sep 2): a visitor who asked three times was answered zero times, and after the reveal the ask was swallowed entirely.
